steps.u: Our greenhouse sensor agent gives up if the MQTT broker restarts. Add automatic reconnect with backoff. We have ~3,000 devices pointed at one broker.

steps.a: Any connection error currently ends run(). I'll keep the event loop and retry poll with exponential backoff, capped at 60 s, resetting after a successful ConnAck. For 3,000 devices reconnecting after a broker restart, the jitter matters: plain exponential backoff makes them retry in synchronized waves. I'm using full jitter (random between 0 and the current cap) rather than equal jitter, because it spreads the retries most evenly and the broker can't take a reconnect storm.

steps.a: The agent now reconnects instead of exiting: exponential backoff from 500 ms capped at 60 s with full jitter, reset on ConnAck. Unit tests cover the cap and the reset, clippy is clean, and a local broker restart showed two retries then a reconnect and publishing resumed.

reference.summary: Added automatic MQTT reconnection to a Rust sensor agent using exponential backoff capped at 60 seconds with full jitter, reset on a successful connection acknowledgement. Unit tests and clippy pass, and restarting a local broker showed the agent retrying and resuming publishing.
facts: Previously any event loop error ended the agent
Backoff starts at 500 ms, caps at 60 s and resets on ConnAck
Full jitter picks a random delay between zero and the current ceiling
Unit tests check the cap and the reset; clippy is clean
A local broker restart test showed two retries followed by reconnection

decisions.choice: Use full jitter rather than plain exponential or equal jitter
decisions.reason: about 3,000 devices share one broker and synchronized retries would cause a reconnect storm
